page: The Microsoft Azure D16as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is supported by 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is included via a 131 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D16as_v4 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, registering a stress-ng single-core score of 2707.98, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21652.21. Memory performance is another highlight, with a strong Passmark memory score of 2783.85, though large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier at 94.0 GB/sec and 50.88 GB/sec respectively. Other workloads, such as Redis SET operations at 16.26 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 14.32 GB/sec, align with average performance expectations.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC hardware, this virtual machine offers a resource-dense and cost-efficient profile for general-purpose enterprise workloads. The inclusion of local SSD storage and Premium Storage compatibility makes it highly suitable for mid-sized databases, web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose business applications. It does not feature GPU acceleration, rendering it unsuitable for heavy deep learning workloads, though it can handle basic, small-scale LLM inference tasks.
